timeline.label: Q2 2026 balance sheet shows $18.9B total debt (current plus non-current lease-adjusted obligations) versus a stale 2012 LongTermDebt tag that had understated leverage by ~$9B.
FY2025 10-K filed: revenue $14.1B (down 3% YoY), operating cash flow $4.6B, capital spending $2.9B.
FY2025 normalized owner earnings $1.71B (operating cash flow minus capital spending) anchors reinvestment DCF proof.
Joe Boitnott became President and CEO after prior leadership transitions; capital allocation and service metrics under new team.
Continued precision-scheduled railroading and industrial development pipeline (~600 projects cited in 2026 proxy) to grow on-network freight.
Activist DFAN14A termination notice on file; prior Mantle Ridge campaign context remains in third-party activist folder.
Surface Transportation Board oversight of Class I mergers and service standards continues to shape Eastern rail competitive structure with Norfolk Southern.
Hunter Harrison-era precision scheduled railroading transformed CSX operating model; legacy efficiency culture persists in investor narrative.

industry.structure: U.S. Class I freight railroad oligopoly in the Eastern U.S.; CSX and Norfolk Southern dominate east-of-Mississippi interchange with high fixed-cost networks and limited new entry.
industry.share_shift: Intermodal and merchandise carloads shift with truck competition and port volumes; CSX gains when on-network industrial development converts to carloads.
industry.trend: Precision scheduled railroading, fuel efficiency, and labor productivity offset cyclical industrial and coal decline; capital spending near $2.9B annually maintains track and equipment.
